title: The Depth Where Direction Learns to Reverse

features.name: gravity well
features.desc-on-touch: A pool where weight has stopped meaning anything. Things sink upward into it. Watching it long enough, you forget which way you are falling.

features.name: inverted tower
features.desc-on-touch: A structure built from the sky downward, or perhaps from the ground up—your eyes cannot decide. It rotates so slowly you only notice the motion when you stop watching.

features.name: rising stone
features.desc-on-touch: A weight that floats. You knew it once, before your memory of up and down corrupted. The stone was your proof that gravity was negotiable.

features.name: descending light
features.desc-on-touch: A glyph that looks like it is falling or rising—it glitches between states so fast that stillness would hurt. Look away before it makes you motion-sick.

features.name: sideways anchor
features.desc-on-touch: An arch that might be holding something down or holding it up. The distinction has become academic. All anchors here are horizontal.

inscription: gravity has forgotten which way is home, and you are learning to follow

file.name: DirectionLost_Log_1989.txt
file.note: Field notes from the inverted chamber. Measurements contradict themselves. 'Up' has become a hypothesis. The archive watches down learn to climb.

exits.label: the way back up into ordinary gravity
toward the chamber where down is still a question

reverie.title: REVERIE — falling or floating underground
narr: You're lying on what was a floor, or is it a ceiling?
Katita reaches toward you but her hand falls upward.
Neither of you moves. Neither is sure which way home.
"Does the stone still remember?" you ask the dark.
She takes your hand. That's the only gravity left.
